name: Latvia
summary: First-time use or possession of a small amount is an administrative offence, not a crime; a repeat after a formal warning is a crime (Criminal Law s.253²). Supply carries long prison terms.

poisonControl.name: Saindēšanās un zāļu informācijas centrs (Poison and Drug Information Centre)

callingForHelp: Since July 2024 the Criminal Law (s.254) exempts from criminal liability for drug use or possession anyone who gives or arranges help to someone overdosing.

lsd.note: First small-amount possession or use is an administrative offence; a repeat after a formal warning is a crime.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin mushrooms count as a narcotic; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat is a crime.

dmt.note: DMT controlled; plants aren't banned, but DMT preparations (ayahuasca) are. First small amount is administrative.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat is a crime.

dox.note: Controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat after warning is a crime.

nbomes.note: Controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat after warning is a crime.

2c-x.note: Controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat after warning is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: Controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat after warning is a crime.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and related tryptamines are controlled (new psychoactive substances also banned); first small amount is administrative.

cannabis.note: First small-amount possession/use is an administrative offence (fines reported up to €280 for ~1 g); a repeat after a formal warning is a crime.

ketamine.note: Controlled medicine: unprescribed small-amount possession is treated like other drugs (administrative first, then criminal).

mxe.note: Controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative, repeat after warning is a crime.

dxm.note: Not verified. DXM is not under the UN drug conventions; whether it is OTC or prescription-only in Latvia was not confirmed.

nitrous.note: Not a controlled drug; national sales rules not verified. EU ban on consumer sales expected from Feb 2027.

amphetamines.note: First small-amount possession is administrative; repeat after warning is a crime. ADHD medicines by prescription.

mdma.note: First small-amount possession is administrative; repeat after warning is a crime.

cocaine.note: First small-amount possession is administrative; repeat after warning is a crime.

caffeine.note: Legal, but selling energy drinks to under-18s has been banned since 2016.

alcohol.note: Legal from 18; buyers aged 18–25 must show ID.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is controlled; first small-amount possession is administrative. Status of GBL/1,4-BD not verified.

opioids.note: Heroin and other opioids: first small-amount possession is administrative; repeat after warning is a crime.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine. Whether unprescribed possession is itself an offence was not verified.

benzodiazepines.note: Psychotropic substances: unprescribed small-amount possession is treated like other drugs.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue not known to be controlled. Ayahuasca preparations are illegal (DMT).
